In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

imatinib is the first drug in the history of medicine that has been proven in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial to be superior to a standard of care, in this case, hydroxyurea, in a chronic disease.
imatinib has been shown to be effective and safe in the majority of patients with chronic phase CML.
the use of TDM for imatinib in CML patients is not recommended at present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of imatinib in CML is associated with a low incidence of severe adverse effects.
we have shown that the pharmacokinetic variability of imatinib is large, that this variability is not related to the clinical response and that the variability is not reduced by dose adjustments.
we were able to demonstrate that the majority of CML patients with imatinib treatment failure had sub-therapeutic imatinib plasma levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TDM of imatinib should not be used to guide treatment decisions, but rather as a means to assess compliance and to detect the presence of drug interactions.
TDM should be considered in patients on imatinibs, especially in those with poor adherence, those who experience toxicity, and those with poor response.

the therapeutic drug monitoring of imatinib in patients with chronic phase CML is a useful strategy for the identification of patients with low imatinib plasma levels and poor compliance to treatment.
